ev.q: The analysis found that the national prevalence of smokefree home rules increased from 43.0% during 1992–1993 to 83.0% during 2010–2011.
Households were considered to have a smokefree home rule if all adult respondents aged ≥18 years
The national prevalence of smokefree home rules increased from 43.0% during 1992–1993 to 83.0% during 2010–2011 (p<0.05)
Among households with no adult smokers, the national prevalence of smokefree home rules increased from 56.7%
CDC analyzed the most recent data from the Tobacco Use Supplement to the Current Population Survey.
To assess progress toward increasing the proportion of households with smokefree home rules

methods_quotes.q: Data were adjusted for nonresponse and weighted using the household supplement self-response weight.
Point estimates and 95% confidence intervals were used to describe the prevalence of smokefree home rules overall and by state.
Differences between groups were assessed using chi-square tests, and logistic regression was used to assess temporal trends (Wald test; p<0.05).
Households with discrepancies in responses (i.e., one respondent reported a smokefree home rule, and another did not) were excluded
